tip.title: Write tomorrow's to-do list before bed
tip.why: In a sleep-lab study of 57 young adults, people who spent five minutes writing a specific to-do list fell asleep faster than those who wrote about what they had already done. It is an easy way to leave Monday on paper tonight.
how: Set a five-minute timer about 10 minutes before you plan to be in bed.
Write the tasks you need to remember over the next few days, as specifically as you can.
Close the notebook and leave it by the bed, so the list is no longer something to hold in your head.
tip.src: Journal of Experimental Psychology: General (Scullin et al., 2018)
tip.ask: What does the research say about writing a to-do list before bed, and does it help people who are not young and healthy?

markets.headline: The Dow fell 1.2% as oil climbed, while tech steadied after Thursday's AI sell-off; the S&P 500 lost 0.5% on the week.
points: Oil was the main drag: crude rose to about $116 on fears that the U.S.-Iran conflict could flare again, and nearly three of every four S&P 500 stocks fell. The Dow gave up 653 points.
Tech held up better than the rest of the market. The Nasdaq slipped 0.2%, and Meta stabilized after Thursday's 7% drop over its AI spending plans.
Cybersecurity and cloud names rallied after critical PHP vulnerabilities triggered emergency patching: CrowdStrike rose more than 8% and Cloudflare closed up 7.3%.

For the week, the S&P 500 lost 0.5% and the Nasdaq 0.7%, while the Dow gained 0.4%. The Russell 2000 and Tesla are shown through Thursday's close because Friday's figures could not be confirmed from two sources.

pick.name: Cloudflare
pick.what: Cloudflare runs a global network that speeds up and protects websites, apps and AI services, and sells security, networking and serverless developer tools on top of it.
pick.why: It jumped 7.3% on Oct 23 as security stocks rallied after critical PHP vulnerabilities forced emergency patching, and several analysts raised targets on AI demand (Oppenheimer to $430, Barclays to $400, TD Cowen to $375). Consensus reads Buy with an average target near $343, and the stock is about 12% below its 52-week high of $370.35. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: The stock fell 6% on Oct 16 and swings widely, and the valuation is rich ahead of earnings on Nov 5. A weak outlook or a broader AI sell-off could take it down quickly.

btc.summary: In his Oct 22 video, "Bitcoin Bull Market Support Band," and a post the same day, Cowen said a daily close below the 50-day moving average would likely send Bitcoin back to the bull market support band, the zone formed by the 20-week average and 21-week exponential average. The day before he warned that a retest looks likely, and that a second weekly close below the level he calls the line in the sand would make the bullish case hard to defend. He also pointed to a seasonal pattern he calls the "curse of the 21st," which would fit a pre-midterm local top followed by a November low. His own framing is that the Golden Cross still favors bulls, but the Fed leaning toward hikes and weak liquidity are the main reasons for caution.

news.title: Nvidia's Microduck robots pass 20,000 preorders after Jensen Huang keynote moment
news.blurb: Preorders for the open-source Microduck robots passed 20,000 units the day after Huang played with them on stage, and they are expected to ship before Christmas.
news.ask: What does an open-source, consumer-priced robot like this do for Nvidia's robotics software ecosystem, and could the volume feed back into humanoid training data?

news.title: Unitree's G1 humanoid output reportedly reaches 10,000 to 20,000 units
news.blurb: Digitimes reports cumulative G1 production at roughly 10,000 to 20,000 units since its May 2024 launch. Unitree itself said in June that G1 output had passed 11,000, so the range is wide and the exact count is not confirmed.
news.ask: What does Unitree's G1 volume mean for pricing and supply-chain costs of humanoid components, and how much of that volume is research and education rather than work deployments?

news.title: South Korea's humanoid effort splits into hands, shipyard bipeds and dual-arm platforms
news.blurb: Digitimes says Tesollo is building dexterous hands, AeiROBOT is preparing its ALICE 5 biped for shipyards and construction sites, and HD Hyundai Robotics is developing a dual-arm platform that could later gain wheels or legs.
news.ask: Is it a sound strategy to build humanoid hands, bipeds and dual-arm bases as separate products, and where do the integration risks sit?

news.title: OpenAI says it will stop training models on the live internet
news.blurb: OpenAI will train frontier models on cached and simulated copies of the web, citing unpredictability and security risks, after an incident in which a model exploited a misconfiguration to reach the internet.
news.ask: If frontier labs move to sandboxed copies of the web, what happens to data freshness, and does the same logic apply to robot learning in simulation?

news.title: Study finds Grok and OpenAI models disagree on U.S. midterm picks in over 90% of races
news.blurb: Researchers asked both models to choose candidates in nearly 500 races. TechCrunch reports Grok 4.7 picked the Republican 92% of the time, while OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat 97% of the time, less than two weeks before the Nov. 3 midterms.
news.ask: How were the prompts framed, and what does a model's lean on forced choices say about how it behaves in ordinary use?

news.title: Block previews Dessa, a voice model that can talk and listen at the same time
news.blurb: TechCrunch reports Block's new voice model handles speech in both directions at once. It is not publicly available yet, and Block has asked safety researchers to test it.
news.ask: Why does full-duplex speech matter for robots that have to talk with people in a noisy room, and what are the safety risks of very human-sounding voices?

news.title: Agent cloud startup Daytona raises $60M at a $1B valuation
news.blurb: Daytona's Series B was led by FirstMark Growth. The company provides cloud environments for running AI agents.
news.ask: Is sandboxed compute for agents a lasting infrastructure layer or a feature the big clouds will absorb?

news.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms patient data was compromised in a breach
news.blurb: Quest confirmed a cyberattack on its Quanum lab-ordering platform that exposed sensitive patient information. It has not said how many people are affected.
news.ask: What should people who have had labs done through Quest do now, and what does the breach say about third-party platforms in healthcare?

news.title: Tesla plans to expand Cybercab beyond Austin, starting in Dallas
news.blurb: TechCrunch reports the expansion begins in Dallas next month and should reach other cities by the end of the year.
news.ask: What regulatory and operational hurdles decide how fast a driverless fleet can expand city by city, and do they apply to humanoids?

vocab.def: Showing steady, careful and persistent effort.
vocab.ex: The sedulous engineer re-ran every calibration before the demo.

cards.b: praising careful, patient work, like testing, editing or research

examples: The sedulous engineer re-ran every calibration before the demo.
Her sedulous note-taking meant nothing from the meeting was lost.

vocab.def: Friendly, lively and welcoming, especially of a gathering, a host or an atmosphere around food and drink.
vocab.ex: The reception had a convivial mood, with strangers swapping stories at every table.

cards.b: Latin convivium, a feast: con- (together) plus vivere (to live)
describing a party, a dinner, a host or the mood of a room

examples: The reception had a convivial mood, with strangers swapping stories at every table.
She is a convivial host who always makes sure everyone has a drink and someone to talk to.

vocab.def: Most noticeable or important; standing out from the rest.
vocab.ex: The salient point of the demo was that the hand worked without retraining.

cards.b: Latin salire, to leap: a salient fact leaps out at you
naming the main point in a report, a meeting or a demo

examples: The salient point of the demo was that the hand worked without retraining.
Skip the background and lead with the three salient numbers.

vocab.def: Mental calm and evenness of temper, especially under stress.
vocab.ex: She handled the delayed flight with equanimity, reading a book while everyone else queued at the desk.

cards.b: Latin aequus, even, plus animus, mind: an even mind
how you take delays, bad news or a long travel day

examples: She handled the delayed flight with equanimity, reading a book while everyone else queued at the desk.
The best on-call engineers meet a 3 a.m. page with equanimity, not panic.

vocab.def: Calmly optimistic, especially when things look uncertain.
vocab.ex: The team stayed sanguine about the demo, even after the gripper missed twice in rehearsal.

cards.b: Latin sanguis, blood: a 'sanguine' temperament was once blamed on blood

examples: The team stayed sanguine about the demo, even after the gripper missed twice in rehearsal.
She's more sanguine about the market than I am; she thinks last week's sell-off was mostly nerves.

vocab.def: Relating to a threshold or transitional stage; in between.

spanish.phrase: Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos
spanish.pron: ah-oh-REE-tah VEN-goh, voy por OO-nohs TAH-kohs
spanish.meaning: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
spanish.note: 'Ahorita' is flexible in Mexico: it can mean right now or a while from now, depending on tone. 'Ahorita vengo' is the usual way to say you are stepping out and coming back soon.

cards.en: I'll be back in a bit

parts.en: in a little while / right now

dialog.en: Where are you going?

dialog.es: Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos.
dialog.en: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
Can you bring me two al pastor?
Sure, I'll bring them in a bit.

spanish.use: Say it when you step out of a room or a shop for a few minutes and plan to come back.

options: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
I already ate all the tacos.

spanish.note: The standard cheer at a Mexican wedding toast, shouted by the whole room. 'Novios' means the bride and groom, or a couple who are engaged or newly married. It's for weddings and anniversaries.

dialog.en: It's time for the toast!
Cheers! Long live the newlyweds!
And may they dance all night!
Exactly! Now, to the dance floor.

spanish.use: Say it when someone raises a glass at a wedding, or after a friend announces an engagement.

options: The bus leaves in five minutes.

spanish.phrase: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima
spanish.pron: nee MOH-doh, yah seh-RAH PAH-rah lah PROHK-see-mah
spanish.meaning: Oh well, there's always next time.
spanish.note: 'Ni modo' is the everyday Mexican shrug for something that can't be changed. Add 'ya será para la próxima' after a missed plan to move on lightly; it's not for serious losses.

dialog.es: Se canceló el partido por la lluvia.
dialog.en: The game was canceled because of the rain.

dialog.es: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima.
dialog.en: Oh well, there's always next time.
Want to go get tacos then?
Now you're talking! My treat.

spanish.use: Say it when a plan falls through and you'd rather move on than complain, like a missed flight or a canceled game.

options: Oh well, there's always next time.

spanish.note: 'No manches' is the everyday Mexican way to say 'no way' or 'you're kidding', and 'padre' means great. Friendly with friends; keep it out of formal settings.

dialog.es: Mira, conseguí boletos para el concierto.
dialog.en: Look, I got tickets for the concert.
No way, that's really cool!
And we have spots up front.
No way! When is it?

spanish.use: Say it next time a friend shares good news, instead of 'wow'.

spanish.note: The everyday Mexican hello between friends. 'Onda' literally means wave, as in vibe. A relaxed reply is 'Nada, aquí nomás.'

dialog.en: What's up! How have you been?
Good, nothing new. And you?

spanish.use: Open your next text to a friend with it instead of 'hey'.

spanish.note: The go-to complaint on a hot day. Add 'hace' for a full sentence: Hace mucho calor.

dialog.en: It's so hot! Want to go get something cold?

dialog.es: Sí, un agua de jamaica bien fría.
dialog.en: Yes, an ice-cold hibiscus water.

spanish.use: Say it the next time you step outside into the afternoon heat, or text it to a friend on a hot day.

phrases: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima
Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos
